lines.text: An Olympic medal chipped his tooth.
Winners bite their medals because photographers ask them to.
The pose copies an old test for gold coins.
Real gold is soft, so a bite leaves a dent.
But Olympic gold medals have not been solid gold since 1912.

post.caption: An Olympic medal chipped his tooth. Winners bite their medals because photographers ask them to. The pose copies an old test for gold coins, because real gold is soft. But Olympic gold medals have not been solid gold since 1912, and London's 2012 gold medals were about 1.34 percent gold. At the 2010 Winter Olympics, German luger David Moeller won silver. Photographers asked the medalists to bite their medals, and he told the paper Bild they wanted his medal between his teeth. A corner of his front tooth broke off.
